newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe to exit Wow! service, take charge.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe to exit Wow! service, take charge.

text.p: CompuServe Corp said it will exit its Wow! service, effective January 31, resulting in a one-time after-tax charge of $4.9 million, or $0.06 a share, for second quarter, in a press release obtained by Reuters.
CompuServe also announced a global strategy, aimed at focusing on its leadership in the business and professional market.

CompuServe said it will continue pursuing growth in the higher-margin European and other international consumer markets. In the U.S. consumer market, it will continue to provide its CSI service and its Internet service, with a focus on retention and growth efforts in its traditional CSI service.
CSI stands for CompuServe Interactive Service.
CompuServe also said it will launch "CompuServe for Business," an enhanced service built on its CSI service with focused content designed for business people and professionals.
CompuServe for Business will be launched early next year. In the same time frame, CompuServe plans to introduce enhanced offerings for the business and professional sector in Europe.

"We will stop undifferentiated marketing to mass consumers,' said CompuServe president and CEO, Bob Massey, in a statement. "Like others in our industry, we were bringing new users in the front door and seeing many go out the back."
"When we launched our WOW! service earlier this year, we felt it was the right product for the time," Massey said. WOW! was introduced in March of this year.

"Since that time, much has changed in terms of market entrants, pricing and the high cost to compete in the mass consumer market. We intend to focus our resources in those sectors where we can profitably expand our business," he said.
Massey said that CompuServe will refocus on its existing leadership among business, professional and technical users, as well as its traditional base of sophisticated consumers.
"This is where we built our name and reputation," he said.
CompuServe was the first of the online services, founded in 1969.

CompuServe also said its Network Services division continued impressive growth in the second quarter. Revenues from its Network Services grew 33 percent over last year's quarter to $63.6 million and represented nearly 30 percent of the company's total revenues of $214.3 million in the quarter.

In the second quarter, CompuServe reported a total loss of $58 million, or $0.63 a share, including special charges for exiting the WOW! service and for amortisation of previously capitalised subscriber acquisition costs.
